Both precipitates white. For Al3+, Pb2+, Zn2+, chloride test (AgNO3) yields white precipitate for all (AgCl). So not discriminating. Hydroxide test: adding KOH yields white precipitate for Al(OH)3 (white gelatinous), Zn(OH)2 (white), Pb(OH)2 (white). So also not discriminating.

We need further tests: maybe ammonium hydroxide test: Al(OH)3 precipitate dissolves in excess NH4OH? Actually Al(OH)3 is amphoteric, dissolves in excess NaOH forming [Al(OH)4]-. Zn(OH)2 also amphoteric dissolves in excess NaOH. Pb(OH)2 is not amphoteric (insoluble in excess NaOH). So we could add NaOH excess to see if precipitate dissolves. But we need NaOH reagent.
